blocks: In this paper, we reviewed several aspects of theoretical and experimental research performed at CQD on InGaAs/InGaP quantum dot infrared photodetectors. We have found that such devices can be fabricated to have a high detectivity, low dark current, and be insensitive to temperature changes. We conclude that quantum dot photodetectors are a promising technology that may eventually surpass quantum well photodetectors, possibly even offering room-temperature operation for solid-state photodetector devices.
